title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1982-04-06
lineage: AUD/fob cm> dat> cdr> eac> shn

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Philly Spectrum show with a smoking Shakedown > Lost Sailor > Terrapin sequence, captured on an audience tape that’s generally good but a bit uneven.
ai_review.review: The concert is remembered as one of the best ’80s East‑Coast shows – the second set erupts with Shakedown Street into Lost Sailor, Saint of Circumstance and Terrapin Station, plus killer moments of The Other One, Morning Dew and Truckin’.  The audience recording (AUD) is praised for its rich, full sound despite occasional level bumps, making the night’s fire and snow‑soaked excitement very listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance 4‑5 stars and highlight multiple standout moments, while recording quality is generally described as good with only occasional flaws; the weighted average yields a strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Rich, full sound with manageable crowd noise; some reviewers note level fluctuations and mild distortion, but overall listenable and better than many SBDs of the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds with classics and Cold Rain & Snow; the second set launches into a fiery Shakedown‑Lost Sailor‑Terrapin suite that keeps momentum high throughout, ending on an uplifting Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soaring lead guitar (“delicious lead”, “rings it out”, “perfect tone”).
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass work – described as “bombing” and standing tall during The Other One.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (piano) receives strong kudos, especially on Shakedown Street and overall piano mode.
